title: role-differentiators-talkbook-ml-backend-platform
content:
Objective:
This is a compact talkbook for GTM teams to run short, role-specific conversations with engineering audiences: ML engineers, backend engineers, and platform teams. Focus: 3–5 minute elevator + 10–15 minute discovery + 2–3 minute close.

Status/context notes:
- Working draft; pulled from recent demos and field feedback (Q4 enterprise trials).
- Emphasize different cost/latency/observability levers per persona rather than generic feature list.
- Includes quick competitive callouts and suggested rebuttals.
- Use as living doc for SDRs, AEs, solutions, and product marketing.

High-level framing (for all roles):
- Core problem: inference reliability & unit economics are a moving target — teams need predictable latency, cost visibility, and simple fallbacks when capacity or model behavior regresses.
- Redwood positioning: production-first inference platform that unifies hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with observable cost/latency controls and rollout primitives.

ML Engineer (primary concerns: model quality, iteration speed, reproducible evals)
- Elevator (30s): "We help ML teams ship model-backed features without re-engineering serving infra — you keep iterating models while we handle predictable latency, KV/prefix caching, and easy versioned rollouts so regressions don't break product."
- Top pain points to surface:
  - "I can't iterate models in prod because rollouts are risky"
  - "Latency regressions after model updates"
  - "Hard to run A/B/eval suites at scale with realistic traffic"
- Key messages + benefits to stress:
  - Model rollouts and canaries: pin versions, canary X% of traffic, automatic fallback to previous compatible model on degradation.
  - Eval integration: tie eval suites to rollout triggers and quality regression alerts.
  - Quantization & model variant recommendations per workload (we suggest tiny-accuracy-preserving variants).
- Quick competitive notes:
  - Versus LLM-API providers: they give you the model but few production rollouts + eval integrations. Sell: integrated evals + rollouts.
  - Versus inference runtimes: they require infra ownership; we offer the same controls as a managed runtime but with optional private deployments.
- Discovery questions:
  - "How do you currently validate model releases before/after rollout?"
  - "What latency SLOs matter per route? Any percentiles we should know?"
- Example two-line script for demos:
  - "Show me your current rollout flow — we’ll demo how to create a canary, run an eval set, and configure auto-fallback in <8 minutes>."

Backend Engineer (primary concerns: latency SLOs, integration simplicity, cost per request)
- Elevator (30s): "We reduce tail latency and per-token cost while preserving dev ergonomics — one API and SDK, predictable throughput across regions, and automatic batching/caching to lower unit costs."
- Top pain points to surface:
  - "Token costs spike during peak usage"
  - "High p99 latency and noisy neighbor issues on shared hosts"
  - "SDK/contract churn across environments"
- Key messages + benefits to stress:
  - Smart routing and policy-based fallbacks (route by latency vs cost vs region).
  - Autoscaling plus dedicated capacity options for predictable throughput.
  - Developer ergonomics: same API across hosted/dedicated/private so integration is one-time.
- Quick competitive notes:
  - Versus cloud AI endpoints: they offer scale but not inference-specific batching/caching optimizations. Sell: workload-aware batching, KV-prefix caching for common patterns (chat/assistant).
  - Versus LLM-API: better cost controls and routing options.
- Discovery questions:
  - "Which routes are most latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive?"
  - "How do you measure unit economics today? Token-based, invocation-based, or hybrid?"
- Demo hook:
  - "Map your busiest route and we’ll show a 20–40% unit-cost delta by enabling caching + batching in <10 minutes>."

Platform Teams (primary concerns: governance, predictable SLAs, multi-team standardization)
- Elevator (30s): "We give platform teams a single control plane to enforce inference SLOs across business units — standard APIs, RBAC, audit logs, and private deployment options for regulated workloads."
- Top pain points to surface:
  - "Fragmented inference runtimes across teams -> inconsistent metrics and SLOs"
  - "Hard to budget for inference spend with noisy adopters"
  - "Compliance and data locality requirements"
- Key messages + benefits to stress:
  - Centralized observability: per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost attribution, and traces tied back to requests.
  - Policy primitives: quotas, per-team routing policies, and canary rollout controls.
  - Private/VPC and on-prem options + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
- Quick competitive notes:
  - Versus managed cloud: lacks enterprise policies and easy migration paths; we provide both managed and private deployment with the same API.
  - Versus self-hosted runtimes: they give control but lack turnkey observability and cost attribution. Sell: operational hygiene + packaged private control plane.
- Discovery questions:
  - "How do you currently enforce SLOs and budgets across teams? Any manual processes?"
  - "Do you have regulatory constraints that require VPC/on-prem or specific KMS?"
- Close script:
  - "We can run a quick audit of one route/team and produce a recommended policy bundle (quotas + a rollout plan) you can test in staging in 1 week."

Competitive shorthand (for quick reps):
- General cloud AI providers: good scale + ecosystem, weak on inference-specific batching/caching and model rollouts.
- LLM-API vendors: fast to start, limited enterprise controls and observability.
- Inference infra vendors/self-hosted: full control but high operational cost and missing packaged evals + cost attribution.
- Our angle: unify the operational primitives (rollouts, caching, routing, observability) across deployment modes so teams get the control of self-hosted + convenience of managed.

Objections + suggested responses (rapid):
- "We already have endpoints in our cloud provider." -> "Great — compare TCO and tail latency on a high-traffic route; many teams see 20–50% lower unit cost after caching/batching and fewer P99 incidents because of our workload-aware kernel selection."
- "We can’t trust managed services with data" -> "Private deployment and VPC options + audit logs and KMS integrations give you parity with in-house infra and a path to migrate incrementally."
- "We care only about model accuracy, not infra" -> "Accuracy is necessary but not sufficient — without rollout/eval hooks and predictable latencies, model regressions leak into product UX and SLOs. We help you test and protect production traffic automatically."

Field collateral + quick assets to attach (suggested):
- 1-pager: "How to reduce inference unit cost by 30% with caching & batching" (attach in demo).
- Short benchmark summary: p50/p95/p99 improvements on common chat patterns vs baseline.
- Canaries checklist for ML teams (template).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need an example eval set that’s representative of a mid-market chat assistant — who owns creation? (Product/Applied ML?)
- Collect anonymized examples of routes (path, qps, avg sequence length) from pilot customers for a public-ish benchmark.
- Request engineering to prepare a short demo recipe that toggles caching/batching and shows cost delta in <8 minutes. (Linked: JIRA-INFER-214)

Next steps for GTM:
- Run 3 internal role-play sessions (SDR/AE/Solutions) to refine scripts and time to demo — target completion 2025-03-16.
- Create slide deck with 2 role-specific one-pagers and the competitive quick-shorts.
- Lock down 1 production route from pilot customer for benchmark write-up.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal):
- Shorten ML script to one live demo flow: model upload -> attach eval set -> create canary -> watch fallback.
- Add callouts about Optimize (quantization suggestions) — platform teams care when budgets are tight.
- Check with security on language for HSM/KMS in the customer-facing one-pager.

References/links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-9876 (persona research notes)
- Jira: JIRA-INFER-214 (demo recipe)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/42 (bench data)

End of draft.

Unpolished / freeform fragments used in meetings:
- "rollouts are the seatbelt for ML"
- "batching silently pays rent"
- "platforms want a single throttle knob for variance"

(If we land this structure, convert to three one-pagers and a short checklist pack.)
